alignments.note: 3ms suffix on תְּפִלָּה rendered by the possessive *His* (rule 18).
Construct noun תְּפִלָּה → *prayer*; the ASV writes no *of*, the suffix being the rectum (rule 19/18).
Opening waw rendered by the postposed *also* (rule 51); the word stands after the fronted subject, and distance from the waw is not evidence against it.
Waw → *and* (rule 14).

Supplied subordinator *how* over a clause whose only conjunction, the waw of s004, already holds the *and* written for it; a waw holding a connective of its own is not a home for a second word (rules 51, 55).
Supplied lexical subject noun *God*, answering to no source morpheme; the ASV italic corroborates without deciding (rules 17, 7).
Niphal infinitive construct עָתַר → *was entreated*, headed on the lexical verb (rule 24).
לְ rendered by the *of* through which the English passive reaches its agent (rule 11).
3ms suffix → object pronoun *him* (rule 18).
Waw → *and* (rule 14).
Quantifying construct כֹּל → *all*; the ASV writes no *of* for the chain, so nothing more is placed (rule 19).
3ms suffix → possessive *his* (rule 18).
חַטָּאת → *sin*.
Waw → *and* (rule 14).
3ms suffix → possessive *his* (rule 18).
מַעַל → *trespass*.
Waw → *and* (rule 14).
Article → *the* (rule 15).
מָקוֹם → *places*.

Relative with its resumptive preposition and 3mp suffix pointing back to *the places*, rendered by the single pronominal adverb *wherein*; the one word carries the relation and the resumption alike, so the three share one unit headed on the relative (rules 22, 30, 23).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun; head on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).
בָּמָה → *high places*, headed on *high*: *places* alone is any place, and the ASV does not write it alone for this word (rule 31).
Waw → *and* (rule 14).
Hiphil of עמד → *set up*; *up* is a phrasal particle completing a lexeme *set* alone does not write, so it joins the verb and the head stays on the verb (rule 44).
Article → *the* (rule 15).
אֲשֵׁרָה (plural) → *Asherim*.
Waw → *and* (rule 14).
Article → *the* (rule 15).
פָּסִיל → *graven images*, headed on *graven* by rule 31's subtraction: *images* alone is any image. The competing reading heading on the noun was available and is set aside on that test.
Preposition on the construct noun פָּנֶה rendered by the single word *before*; the pair fuses, headed on the construct noun (rule 30).
Suffix on the infinitive construct is its subject and takes the English subject pronoun *he* (rule 18).
Niphal infinitive construct כנע → *humbled himself*; the reflexive renders the verb's own voice and stays in its unit, headed on the lexical verb (rule 44).
הִנֵּה → *behold* (rule 11).
3mp suffix on הִנֵּה realized by the subject pronoun *they* (rule 18).
Passive participle with the copula the construction supplies, headed on the lexical predicate (rules 20, 24).
עַל rendered *in* by the ASV's printed text (rule 11).
Construct דִּבְרֵי → *the history*; no article morpheme stands in the chain, so the supplied *the* joins the construct noun (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the chain's relational *of* together with its own word, headed on the name (rules 19, 24). The margin's *Or, the seers* was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).

review_notes: The verse's two supplied words in the second clause are marked separately: *how* is a subordinator over a clause whose waw already holds *and*, and *God* is a supplied lexical subject; the ASV italic on *God* corroborates only.
אֲשֶׁר with בָהֶם is read as one *wherein* fusion (rules 22, 30) rather than a rendered relative beside an unrepresented suffix.
Head choices on *high places* and *graven images* follow rule 31's subtraction test; the alternative of heading each on its English noun was considered and rejected.
